svg.text: Two ways to trade a trapped crowd
Both are longs. Both wait for someone else’s stop to be taken. RSO waits for PROOF before entering; ELS acts AT the level.
They broke it. They got shaken out. Then it broke for real — and you take the second break.
early buyers’ stops sit under it
under the lowest low of A→C
wick under the origin — the shake out
A level fills with orders. Price comes and empties it. You buy as it empties.
takes an old low → longs only
minor high taken — more buyers pile in
a high that respects & leaves → THE TARGET
The one line that separates them
RSO needs a second break before you are allowed in. ELS puts you in on the sweep itself. Same trapped crowd, different amount of patience.
ExternalEvents on 4H · last label HL / LH
Long only while price ≤ the 0.5 of the 4H leg
A wick drops UNDER that origin. Those buyers are out
Under the lowest low between A and C
Price takes an old low from the left → longs only
A low returns, HOLDS, and leaves → it is now loaded
A minor high gets taken. More buyers pile in
A high respects earlier highs then leaves → the EL
Price sweeps the loaded low → buy the stab
Past the liquidity block (the arming leg’s extreme)
No EL built = NO TRADE. This is the step people skip
Schematic, not a replay. ELS long side measured 2026-08-13: 49 trades, 34.7% vs a matched random 22.9%, z +1.96 — marginal, and the short side had no edge. RSO has a full spec and no code yet.
